flatfish serve#

Start a local development server to preview your site.

Usage#

flatfish serve [options]

Options#

Option

Short

Description

Default

--port

-p

Port number

8000

--host

-h

Host address

localhost

--open

-o

Open browser automatically

False

--watch

-w

Watch for changes

True

--directory

-d

Site directory

site/

What It Does#

The serve command:

  1. Starts a local HTTP server

  2. Serves your generated site

  3. Optionally watches for changes

  4. Provides live reload

Examples#

Basic Server#

flatfish serve
# Server running at http://localhost:8000

Custom Port#

flatfish serve --port 3000
# Server running at http://localhost:3000

Open Browser Automatically#

flatfish serve --open
# Opens http://localhost:8000 in default browser

Network Access#

flatfish serve --host 0.0.0.0
# Server accessible from other devices on network

Different Directory#

flatfish serve --directory public/

Live Reload#

When --watch is enabled (default):

Flatfish Serve
══════════════

Server running at http://localhost:8000

Watching for changes...
  • transcriptions/
  • entities/
  • output/
  • templates/

[10:30:15] Changed: output/timeline.txt
[10:30:15] Rebuilding affected pages...
[10:30:16] ✓ 3 pages updated
[10:30:16] Browser reloaded

Watched Paths#

By default, watches:

  • transcriptions/ - Document content

  • entities/ - Entity data

  • output/ - Summary files

  • templates/ - Custom templates

  • flatfish.yaml - Configuration

Disable Watch#

flatfish serve --no-watch

Development Workflow#

Typical Session#

# Terminal 1: Run server
flatfish serve --open

# Terminal 2: Make changes
# Edit templates, update config, etc.
# Browser auto-refreshes

Quick Iteration#

  1. Start server with watch

  2. Edit flatfish.yaml or templates

  3. See changes immediately

  4. Repeat until satisfied

  5. Deploy when ready

Request Logging#

Each request shows:

  • Timestamp

  • HTTP method

  • Path

  • Status code

Configuration#

flatfish.yaml Settings#

serve:
  # Default port
  port: 8000
  
  # Open browser on start
  open_browser: false
  
  # Enable live reload
  live_reload: true
  
  # Paths to watch
  watch_paths:
    - "transcriptions/"
    - "entities/"
    - "output/"
    - "templates/"

Accessing from Other Devices#

Local Network#

flatfish serve --host 0.0.0.0

Find your IP:

# macOS/Linux
ip addr | grep inet
# or
hostname -I

# Windows
ipconfig

Access from other device:

http://192.168.1.100:8000

Tunneling (ngrok)#

For external access:

# Install ngrok
# https://ngrok.com/

# Start server
flatfish serve

# In another terminal
ngrok http 8000
# Gives public URL like https://abc123.ngrok.io

Troubleshooting#

Port Already in Use#

Error: Port 8000 already in use

Solution:

# Use different port
flatfish serve --port 8001

# Or find and kill existing process
lsof -i :8000
kill <PID>

Watch Not Working#

# Increase watch limit (Linux)
echo fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288 | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf
sudo sysctl -p

Slow Reload#

For large sites, limit watched paths:

serve:
  watch_paths:
    - "templates/"  # Only watch templates
